newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma wants foreigners to own land.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma wants foreigners to own land.

text.p: Ukraine should open up agricultural privatisation to foreigners and give them the right to own land where they run businesses to boost direct foreign investment, President Leonid Kuchma said on Friday.
"Ukraine has not been attracting foreign investors," Kuchma told government and parliament in his annual address to the nation broadcast live to 51 million Ukrainians.
"We must let investors buy land and invest in privatisation in the agriculture sector," Kuchma added during a section of the almost 90-minute speech on the problems of foreign investment.
He listed several laws which should be amended, including the land code, which should "give foreign investors the right to portions of land they use in their businesses".
Conservative deputies who oppose foreigners owning land -- a law has not been passed for Ukrainians to own it -- booed him as he spoke.
A majority of deputies would have to approve such a law if it was proposed by government.

The former Soviet republic has attracted only $1.4 billion in foreign investment since independence in 1991, with investors complaining most about uncooperative bureaucrats, demands for bribes, punishing taxes, and inconsistent laws as deterrents.

Roman Shpek, chief of the National Agency of Ukraine for Reconstruction and Development, told reporters outside parliament that foreign investment this year would double to $900 million from $450 million in 1996.
Kuchma said a "chain of barriers" existed to foreign investors and blamed bureaucrats who wanted to preserve the old order for many of the problems.

"AvtoZAZ is dying because of a lack of financial resources," he said of the car-maker based in the eastern industrial city of Zaporizhya. "It has gone from producing 124,000 vehicles per year to 7,000."
U.S. carmaker General Motors and South Korea's Daewoo Group have been competing to invest in the plant but must wait until the government makes a decision, due this month.
